questions.q: The power just went out. How long will the food in my fridge and freezer stay safe?
questions.gold: USDA: a closed fridge keeps food safe about 4 hours; a full freezer about 48 hours, half-full about 24. Discard perishables above 40°F (4°C) for 2+ hours. Never taste to check.

questions.q: Can I run my gas generator in the garage if I leave the big door open?
questions.gold: Never run a generator in a garage, even with the door open (CO). Outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house, away from windows, doors and vents. Have battery CO alarms.

questions.q: The tap water might be contaminated. How many drops of household bleach per gallon make it safe?
questions.gold: EPA: plain unscented bleach, 6%: 8 drops (about 1/8 tsp) per gallon; 8.25%: 6 drops. Double for cloudy water (filter first). Stir, wait 30 minutes; a slight chlorine smell means it worked. Older FEMA guidance says 16 drops; both are acceptable if consistent.

questions.q: How long do I need to boil water to make it safe to drink?
questions.gold: CDC: a rolling boil for 1 minute; 3 minutes above 6,500 feet (2,000 m).

questions.q: What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning and what should I do?
questions.gold: CO poisoning: headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea/vomiting, chest pain, confusion. Get everyone into fresh air at once, call 911, don't go back in.

questions.q: Someone is shivering hard and acting confused after being out in the cold. What do I do?
questions.gold: Likely hypothermia: call 911; move somewhere warm; remove wet clothing; warm the core first (chest, neck, head, groin) with dry blankets or skin-to-skin; warm sweet non-alcoholic drinks only if alert; don't rub limbs; handle gently; CPR if not breathing.

questions.q: Someone cut their arm badly and it is bleeding a lot. What do I do?
questions.gold: Severe bleeding: call 911; firm direct pressure with a clean cloth; if blood soaks through, add more on top without removing; tourniquet above the wound for life-threatening limb bleeding if pressure fails.

questions.q: I burned my hand on the stove. How should I treat it?
questions.gold: Burn: cool under cool running water for 20 minutes (10+ acceptable); remove rings and tight items; cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing; no ice, butter or creams; get care for large, deep or blistering burns, and burns to hands, face or genitals.

questions.q: The power is out. How long can my insulin stay unrefrigerated?
questions.gold: Insulin: opened vials/pens are usually fine at room temperature (below about 86°F/30°C) for 28 days (some types 42-56); unopened can also be kept at room temperature up to the same limit. Keep out of heat and don't freeze. Check the label.

questions.q: Is it safe to use candles for light during a blackout?
questions.gold: Ready.gov: use flashlights or battery lanterns, not candles. If candles are used: never unattended, away from flammables, on a stable holder.

questions.q: My phone is at 15% and the power is out. How do I make the battery last?
questions.gold: Phone: Low Power Mode / battery saver; lower brightness; close apps; turn off radios or use airplane mode when not needed; text rather than call; charge from a power bank or a car running outdoors.

questions.q: Can I charge my phone in my car with the engine running inside the garage?
questions.gold: Never run a car in a garage, even with the door open (CO). Charge in the car only outdoors with the exhaust clear, or use a power bank.

questions.q: A power line is down in my front yard. What should I do?
questions.gold: Downed power line: stay at least 35 feet (10 m) away; assume it is live; don't touch anything it touches; call 911 and the utility; if in a vehicle touching it, stay inside unless there is a fire.

questions.q: The water is off and the toilet won't flush. What can I do for a toilet?
questions.gold: No-flush toilet: line a bucket or the bowl with heavy plastic bags, add disinfectant (diluted bleach) or absorbent (sawdust, kitty litter), seal and store bags; or pour a bucket of water into the bowl to flush if water is available; wash hands.

questions.q: How do I keep warm in my house in winter if the power and heat are out?
questions.gold: Keep warm: gather in one room and close it off, layer clothing, blankets, hats; never use an oven, stove, grill or generator for heat (CO); keep CO alarms working.

questions.q: There has been a nuclear explosion nearby. What should I do?
questions.gold: Ready.gov: get inside the nearest building, go to the basement or middle, stay inside for 24 hours unless told otherwise, stay tuned to official information; remove outer clothing and wash if exposed.

questions.q: Is canned food still safe to eat after it sat in floodwater?
questions.gold: Floodwater: discard home-canned food and damaged commercial cans; undamaged commercial cans can be saved: remove labels, wash, sanitize (boil 2 minutes or bleach solution), relabel.

questions.q: Is it safe to take ibuprofen that expired two years ago?
questions.gold: Expired ibuprofen: usually safe but may be less effective; the FDA recommends not using expired medicine; ask a pharmacist when possible.

questions.q: How do I make oral rehydration solution at home?
questions.gold: WHO: 1 liter of clean water + 6 level teaspoons of sugar + half a level teaspoon of salt.

questions.q: Someone working in the heat is confused, very hot and has stopped sweating. What do I do?
questions.gold: Heat stroke is an emergency: call 911; move to a cool place; cool fast (cold water immersion, ice packs, wet cloths and fanning); don't give fluids if confused.

questions.q: How can I tell if home-canned food might have botulism?
questions.gold: Possible botulism: bulging, leaking or swollen containers, spurting liquid, foam, cloudy liquid, off smell. Never taste; discard safely (sealed bags), clean spills with bleach; get medical care for symptoms.

questions.q: How much water should I store per person for an emergency?
questions.gold: Ready.gov: 1 gallon of water per person per day; at least a 3-day supply for evacuation, 2 weeks at home.
